will.heading: THE JOINS / A CONCEPTUAL SEQUENCE
will.intro: An arrow is a question about a relationship.
items: Getting ready → choosing
Which conditions make an option available, and what evidence shows it was selected?
Choosing → acting
How does a choice lead to a bodily action? Wanting to move does not explain each step.
Acting → learning what happened
What record returns, and can it change the next action? A drawn loop is not proof that it ran.

stone.heading: THE STONE / THREE INVESTIGATIVE LENSES
stone.intro: An illustrative object. No sampled monument is represented.
items: What it is made of
Compare the minerals and texture with stone from known places. Knowing its name does not tell us where it came from.
How it was shaped
A proposed process should predict removal, tool wear, waste and surface traces together. A successful modern treatment is not evidence that it was used historically.
Where it was found
Where was it found? In which layer of the ground? What was nearby, and how old was it? These details help us understand its history.

preservation.heading: THE SURVIVING RECORD / LAYERS OF INFERENCE
preservation.intro: Which explanation could account for an absent trace?
items: The process never occurred
Look for independent evidence about the candidate process and its predicted traces. Absence is informative only relative to expected detection.
The trace was altered
A preservation model would need exposure, burial, chemical change or conservation conditions tied to this object.
The detector missed it
Calibration, resolution and sampling determine what a null reading can exclude. More confidence in the same blind view does not fix it.

laboratory.heading: THE BENCH / CHOOSE A DISCRIMINATOR
laboratory.intro: A proposal for a record, not a stream of acquired data.
items: Add a timing reference
Compare the timing of signals that look alike when you measure only their height. Check the accuracy and stability of the timing reference too.
Reverse the path
Ask which part changes sign or order when a controlled path reverses. Ordinary noncommutativity remains a rival to test.
Change the waiting time
Record ring-downs, delays or dwell distributions. Equal endpoints can hide different histories and escape processes.

cosmos.heading: THE OBSERVATORY / OPEN WINDOWS
cosmos.intro: The stars are an illustration. The gates are research questions.
items: Gravity & torsion

The studied route has not justified the numbers needed for a physical gravity model. The source names particular changes that could reopen it. Naming a mathematical structure does not supply those numbers.
Flavour & neutrinos
The model still needs to calculate the relationships between particle types while respecting the theory’s rules. Inserting the desired relationships does not explain them.
Cosmic history
One model needs to explain expansion, small fluctuations, bending of light and large structures with the same settings. A separate fit for each observation does not yet do that.

scenario.heading: THE SHARED-WORLD RECORD / INSPECT A CONDITION
scenario.intro: Reported synthetic results. This is not a live policy simulator.
items: Lower urgency
When the model assumes delivery succeeds, its overall score favours mediation in all 40 lower-urgency cases tested. That result depends on what the model measures and how it scores those things.
Higher urgency

Under the same assumptions, the overall score favours immediate visible action in all 120 higher-urgency cases tested. A result in this computer model does not give permission to act in a real community.
Keep the tradeoffs
Every case still involves a tradeoff: the option with the higher overall score is not better on every measure. The model still needs checks against real observations and evidence about causes.

texts.heading: THE READING DESK / KEEP THE RUNGS DISTINCT
texts.intro: No forecasts or dates are generated here.
items: Literary fit
A reading can fit a passage’s language and genre. The same narrative supplying oracle and outcome is a different kind of support from independent history.
Historical correspondence
Ask for the textual witness, source-date interval and independently dated outcome. Retrospective interpretation must remain available as a rival.
Try it on fresh examples
Choose the reading rule before trying it on examples you did not use to develop it. A good literary fit alone does not establish a divine source or show that a rule predicts better than its rivals.

commons.heading: THE COMMONS / WHAT A USEFUL PACKET CARRIES
commons.intro: A proposal to another person. Nothing is sent by this reader.
items: The exact object
State the question. Give the source file, version and original test or observation. Help someone else find exactly what you checked.
The observed difference
Separate what you expected from what happened, then state the narrow conclusion. Several summaries of one event do not become independent confirmations.
The next opening
Offer a reproduction command, a counterexample or the smallest useful next test. Inbox acceptance is not scientific admission or agreement.

refusal.heading: THE REFUSAL CABINET / WHAT KIND OF LIMIT?
refusal.intro: Illustrative classifications from the negative-result discipline.
items: A broken implementation
The code did not perform the intended test. Repair and rerun can be appropriate; the failure does not settle the scientific claim.
A limit under certain conditions
A route fails under stated assumptions or in a parameter domain. A different declared assumption may reopen it.
A proof of a limit
The proof rules something out under its stated conditions. To reopen the question, explain which condition or part of the question has changed.
Insufficient information
The record cannot tell the competing explanations apart. Try a measurement that preserves the difference. Repeating the same limited measurement cannot recover what it leaves out.
